configuration_fact_check.scope: Declared classifier versus the fitted estimator of this trial

proposal.reason: Trial 1 on the primary split used word features with C=0.3 and achieved macro_f1 0.4984, with ham recall 1.0 but spam recall 0.0303. Macro_f1 is therefore limited by the spam class. A char n-gram representation is a distinct route that can capture subword patterns in spam messages; C=3.0 tests less regularization than the completed word baseline.
proposal.review: Only one completed primary trial is available. It shows severe minority-class under-recall, so a representation and regularization change is more informative than repeating the same word C=0.3 configuration. No formal test is available.
proposal.hypothesis: Char n-gram features with logistic regression may capture spam-specific character patterns and improve spam recall relative to the word C=0.3 baseline, potentially raising macro_f1; this is a hypothesis, not a guaranteed improvement.
proposal.uncertainty: There is only one primary trial and no formal test. The direction and magnitude of macro_f1 change are unknown; char features may overfit or may not fix the spam-recall deficit. The comparison is on the primary search split only.
